desk.why: Implied is only 0.88x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs.

facts: NIFTY moved +1.4% over the last 7 sessions and +0.6% on the day, to 25,502.
Almost no gap (-41 pts): the +315-pt body was built during the session, which is stronger evidence than an overnight jump.
The day closed at its high (close - low 397, high - close 6).
India VIX 16.35 (+5.0%) - rising on an up day: traders are paying for protection, the rally is nervous.
ATM IV sits in its 66th percentile of the past year: option premium is middling.

base.why: No trend worth leaning on (7-session move +1.4%), so the plan sells both sides at the writers' walls, 25,400 and 26,000, and lets time decay work. Note: the desk's volatility rule says stand aside today (Implied is only 0.88x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs.). This plan overrides it only for the scenario branches; size down.
text: bull put spread: sell 25,000 PE, buy 24,800 PE (credit about 26 pts, Rs 1,674 per lot; max loss Rs 11,326)
bear call spread: sell 26,400 CE, buy 26,600 CE

Close near the day's high again

If it spikes past 26,400 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.

scenarios.title: Falls to 25,400 and holds
watch: 25,400 PE open interest still rising (put writers defending)
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep today's position, or add nothing (weekly). If it breaks: close today's position and switch to sell 25,400 CE / buy 25,600 CE (weekly). Exact strikes for every expiry are in the position matrix.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,400 in 69.1% of past cases (normal 65.9%).

scenarios.title: Breaks down below 25,400
watch: 25,400 PE open interest falling (put writers exiting)
scenarios.means: The floor gave way. Next: 25,300 then 25,200.
scenarios.action: Close today's position. It would be about Rs 309 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell a spread, sell 25,400 CE / buy 25,600 CE. The old floor 25,400 becomes the ceiling: sell calls at it. Or buy a spread: buy 25,400 PE / sell 25,000 PE.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,300 in 62.3% of past cases (normal 56.7%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
